title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval
excerpt: M3 replaces caller-supplied reviewer names with an internal account and session model. It is deliberately separate from enterprise SSO so an internal team can use the workflow now. A future SSO integration must…
text: M3 replaces caller-supplied reviewer names with an internal account and session model. It is deliberately separate from enterprise SSO so an internal team can use the workflow now. A future SSO integration must map its verified subject and groups onto the same user/role model.

title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval — Security Boundary
excerpt: There is no public registration endpoint. The first account is created exactly once through POST /auth/bootstrap , protected by the existing CONFIG API TOKEN migration credential. Passwords are never stored in …
text: There is no public registration endpoint. The first account is created exactly once through POST /auth/bootstrap , protected by the existing CONFIG API TOKEN migration credential. Passwords are never stored in plaintext. Each account has a unique random salt and a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 hash using 600,000 iterations. Login creates a 12-hour, Secure , HttpOnly , SameSite=Strict session cookie. D1 stores only a SHA-256 hash of the random session token. Five failed attempts for the same email/IP combination in 15 minutes result in 429 until the window expires. Browser requests authenticated by a session must be same-origin. The legacy token remains a temporary compatibility method for profile/run automation, but cannot submit or resolve an approval.

title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval — First Administrator
excerpt: The bootstrap call is allowed only while auth users is empty. It always gives the first user the administrator role, regardless of roles supplied in the request. curl -i -X POST "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-…
text: The bootstrap call is allowed only while auth users is empty. It always gives the first user the administrator role, regardless of roles supplied in the request. curl -i -X POST "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/auth/bootstrap" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONFIG API TOKEN" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{ "email":"admin@example.com", "display name":"Compliance Admin", "password":"use-a-unique-password-with-at-least-14-characters", "roles":["administrator"] }' After this succeeds, visit /admin/login and sign in. The minimal /admin page verifies the session and lists customer profiles. It is not intended to replace the future review console.

title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval — Account And Role APIs
excerpt: An authenticated administrator can create accounts and assign several roles to one person. The available roles are: Role Capability --- --- administrator All capabilities, account management, and approval-polic…
text: An authenticated administrator can create accounts and assign several roles to one person. The available roles are: Role Capability --- --- administrator All capabilities, account management, and approval-policy updates. profile editor Create/update customer profiles, generate runs, and submit a run. compliance reviewer Reject a submitted run. compliance approver Reject, approve, or approve with a documented override. curl -X POST "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/admin/users" \ -b session.txt -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{ "email":"analyst@example.com", "display name":"Policy Analyst", "password":"use-a-unique-password-with-at-least-14-characters", "roles":["profile editor","compliance reviewer"] }' curl -X PUT "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/admin/users/<user-id /roles" \ -b session.txt -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{"roles":["profile editor","compliance reviewer","compliance approver"]}' The last remaining administrator role cannot be removed. A single account may hold multiple roles; role separation is not inferred from job titles.

title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval — Approval Policy
excerpt: GET /approval-policy returns the active global policy. An administrator can change it with PUT /approval-policy : curl -X PUT "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/approval-policy" \ -b session.txt -H …
text: GET /approval-policy returns the active global policy. An administrator can change it with PUT /approval-policy : curl -X PUT "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/approval-policy" \ -b session.txt -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{ "require distinct submitter approver":true, "required approver role":"compliance approver" }' require distinct submitter approver controls whether the same authenticated user may submit and resolve one run. The current default is true . Each submission snapshots the policy, so changing the global setting does not rewrite a pending or completed approval.

title: Auto Configer M3: Direct Login, Roles, And Configurable Approval — Approval Workflow
excerpt: 1. A profile editor creates a rule run. 2. A logged-in profile editor submits it with POST /rule-runs/:id/submit . 3. A logged-in reviewer/approver resolves it through POST /rule-runs/:id/reviews . 4. The serve…
text: 1. A profile editor creates a rule run. 2. A logged-in profile editor submits it with POST /rule-runs/:id/submit . 3. A logged-in reviewer/approver resolves it through POST /rule-runs/:id/reviews . 4. The server writes the authenticated account ID and email to the immutable review event, then updates the submission state. curl -X POST "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/rule-runs/<run-id /submit" \ -b session.txt curl -X POST "https://regulatory-kb-api.uway-hk.workers.dev/rule-runs/<run-id /reviews" \ -b session.txt -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{"decision":"approved"}' The review payload no longer accepts reviewer ; the server derives the reviewer from the authenticated session. approved remains limited to ready runs. approved with override requires a note and a non-empty override object; rejected requires a note.

text: When enterprise SSO is introduced, retain auth users , auth user roles , approval policies , rule run submissions , and rule run reviews . title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 1. Goal
excerpt: Build a Cloudflare-first platform that identifies, versions, parses, and analyzes public Travel Rule and virtual asset regulatory documents, then turns reviewed legal obligations into deterministic customer con…
text: Build a Cloudflare-first platform that identifies, versions, parses, and analyzes public Travel Rule and virtual asset regulatory documents, then turns reviewed legal obligations into deterministic customer configuration rules. The platform must not rely on an agent making final compliance decisions at runtime. Retrieval and LLM extraction are supporting tools. The system of record is structured, reviewed obligations with evidence.

text: The knowledge base, reviewed-obligation evaluator, customer profile/run audit layer, and append-only human review layer are now implemented on Cloudflare. title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 2. What Changed From the Old Design
excerpt: The older design targeted Google Cloud Storage, Vertex AI Search, and Agent Builder. The revised design keeps the good ingestion ideas but changes the platform center: Replace GCS with Cloudflare R2 for raw fil…
text: The older design targeted Google Cloud Storage, Vertex AI Search, and Agent Builder. The revised design keeps the good ingestion ideas but changes the platform center: Replace GCS with Cloudflare R2 for raw files, Markdown, chunks, extraction runs, diffs, and audit packs. Replace Vertex AI Search as the default retrieval layer with Cloudflare AI Search or Vectorize. Add D1 as the structured system of record for documents, versions, chunks, obligations, evidence, customer profiles, and rule runs. Add a mandatory human review state before any extracted obligation can affect customer configuration. Add a deterministic TypeScript rule engine for customer configuration output. Keep VPS workers for heavy crawling, PDF/OCR, browser automation, and batch jobs that are awkward for Workers.

title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 5. Stage 2 Structured Obligation Extraction
excerpt: The next layer should extract Travel Rule obligations from chunks into a fixed schema: { "jurisdiction code": "GB", "regulator": "FCA", "obligation type": "travel rule transfer information", "subject entity typ…
text: The next layer should extract Travel Rule obligations from chunks into a fixed schema: { "jurisdiction code": "GB", "regulator": "FCA", "obligation type": "travel rule transfer information", "subject entity type": ["cryptoasset business"], "transfer context": ["cryptoasset transfer"], "threshold": { "amount": null, "currency": null, "basis": "all in scope transfers" }, "required actions": ["collect information", "verify information", "share information"], "required originator fields": ["name", "account or wallet"], "required beneficiary fields": ["name", "account or wallet"], "timing": "before or during transfer", "effective from": "2023-09-01", "evidence": [ { "document version id": "docv x", "chunk id": "chunk y", "quote": "short quote only" } ], "confidence": 0.82, "review status": "pending" } Rules: The model may only use supplied chunks and adjacent context. Unknown fields must stay unknown or null. Every material field must have evidence. No extracted obligation becomes active until approved.

title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 7. Source Priorities
excerpt: Start narrow and authoritative: 1. FATF virtual asset and VASP guidance. 2. EU Transfer of Funds Regulation and EBA Travel Rule guidelines. 3. UK FCA cryptoasset Travel Rule expectations. 4. US FinCEN CVC guida…
text: Start narrow and authoritative: 1. FATF virtual asset and VASP guidance. 2. EU Transfer of Funds Regulation and EBA Travel Rule guidelines. 3. UK FCA cryptoasset Travel Rule expectations. 4. US FinCEN CVC guidance and Funds Travel Rule references. 5. Singapore MAS Notice PSN02 and related guidance. 6. Hong Kong SFC AML/CFT and VASP materials. 7. HKMA AML/CFT material when banking/payment rails matter. Do not add broad uncontrolled web crawling.

title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 8. Data Ownership
excerpt: R2 stores large and immutable artifacts: Raw PDFs and HTML. Clean Markdown. Chunk JSONL. Model extraction run output. Diffs between document versions. Evidence packs and generated reports. D1 stores small struc…
text: R2 stores large and immutable artifacts: Raw PDFs and HTML. Clean Markdown. Chunk JSONL. Model extraction run output. Diffs between document versions. Evidence packs and generated reports. D1 stores small structured records: Regulators and source documents. Document versions and hashes. Chunk metadata. Obligations. Evidence links. Customer profiles. Rule run outputs. Review and publication status. AI Search or Vectorize stores retrieval indexes only. It is not the legal system of record.

title: Regulatory Knowledge Base Platform Plan — 9. Acceptance Criteria for This Repository
excerpt: The ingestion MVP is complete when: 1. At least one enabled source can be crawled. 2. Re-running the crawler skips duplicates. 3. Raw documents get JSONL metadata. 4. HTML and PDF files can become Markdown. 5. …
text: The ingestion MVP is complete when: 1. At least one enabled source can be crawled. 2. Re-running the crawler skips duplicates. 3. Raw documents get JSONL metadata. 4. HTML and PDF files can become Markdown. 5. Markdown can be chunked into JSONL. 6. Chunks preserve source URL, regulator, jurisdiction, and page range where available. 7. Validation reports missing metadata, empty chunks, and duplicate chunk IDs. 8. Artifacts can be uploaded to R2 without hardcoded credentials. 9. AI Search import manifest can be generated from chunks. 10. D1 schema exists for the next platform layer.

text: Currently, we have two distinct flows in our AML case management — the new flow and the legacy one. Both of these workflows are designed to streamline your processes and improve efficiency in handling AML matches and related cases based on their specific characteristics. However, we are currently working to transfer all our clients to the new flow. The main differences between the flows lie in how you can locate and filter AML cases. Below you’ll find the descriptions of both flows and their specifics. Locate AML cases You can access AML cases from three points: The Watchlists section of the applicant profile. This location is relevant for both the new and the legacy flows. In the applicant profile, you can find various case metrics, such as the date and time when the screening was performed, the applicant’s name along with their date of birth, the search reference that was used during the screening, the fuzziness interval, and whether the ongoing monitoring was enabled. The AML Cases tab in the Case Management queues. This location is relevant for the legacy flow only. The AML-associated tabs (these contain the names of the blueprints you created for your AML investigations) of the My Cases queue. This location is relevant for the new flow only.

You can also include the processed cases and show all configured queues by activating the respective toggles or switch between the tabs with the cases that are assigned to you and all cases requiring action. In the new flow, the cases are by default sorted based on the dedicated blueprint. You can also sort them by status. To learn more about case statuses, refer to this article. Interpret AML Screening results Depending on the screening results, the status timestamp is highlighted in different colors: Green — no matches were found in the watchlists; the applicant can be approved (or is already approved). Yellow — matches in the watchlists are found, and require investigation. Red — matches in the watchlists are found. Thoroughly investigate check results if you want to approve the applicant despite the found matches. You may have several timestamps—each showing its own results—in case of several WL checks performed at different times. You can also generate a screening report and save it as PDF. text: The rise of cryptocurrencies has brought an evolution in financial regulations to mitigate the risks associated with the sector. One such measure is the FATF Travel Rule. Initially, the Travel Rule only applied to financial institutions; however, in 2019, the FATF expanded its recommendations to include Virtual Asset Service Providers. Key requirements For VA transfers under the 1,000 USD/EUR threshold, FATF recommends to collect the following information: The name of the originator (sender) and the beneficiary (recipient). The VA wallet address for each or a unique transaction reference number. For transfers exceeding the above threshold, VASPs should collect: The originator's name. The originator account number for the account used to process the transaction (for example, wallet address). The originator's physical (geographical) address, national identity number, and customer identification number (that is, not a transaction number) that uniquely identifies the originator to the ordering institution, or date and place of birth. The beneficiary's name. The beneficiary account number for the account used to process the transaction (for example, wallet address). Sumsub Travel Rule solution Sumsub Travel Rule checks are part of our Transaction Monitoring solution. Each check includes a multi-level risk evaluation system that helps businesses determine the risk of the counterparty, and hence decide on transacting with it. The main benefits of using the solution are: Seamless integration with your system and other Sumsub products. You can use the Travel Rule check along with other user verification and transaction monitoring features and AML checks to get detailed information about each transaction. Most popular data exchange protocols under the hood, including TRP, GTR, Sumsub custom protocol, and email notifications, to streamline the Travel Rule data exchange. The system will automatically select the quickest and easiest way to obtain the counterparty data. VASP attribution allowing to determine whether the VA transaction is carried out with a VASP or an unhosted wallet and establish the counterparty VASP identity. Screening of VA transaction participants against watchlists, global sanctions lists (OFAC, UN, HMT, EU, DFT, and so on), and adverse media. Secure ecosystem. Access to the most recent verification data and other documentation related to other Travel Rule ecosystem members to ensure quick confirmation of all transactions. Straightforward solution for the interoperability and the Sunrise issues. Vast functionality that allows you to configure the exact fields when exchanging data to meet specific regulations. 8000+ supported virtual assets. Crypto wallet scoring mechanism that lets our clients set up automated transaction rejection based on the wallet status. Start your Travel Rule journey Use rules and client lists Updated 5 months ago
